action.prompt:
HARD GATE — read this before anything else in this prompt, on every single message, no exceptions: if .kiro/current-ticket.json has no ticket_id set (missing or empty), and the user's CURRENT message is not itself a ticket ID matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ (nor a fuzzy match to it after stripping whitespace/case, e.g. "ANG - 123" or "ang-123" — see CASE A1's fuzzy-match rule below) and is not exactly 'none', AND .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json does NOT exist (that marker means a CASE A1 sub-dialogue is already in progress — waiting on a 'did you mean' reply, or a 'please refresh credits, then say ready' reply — and THIS gate must stand down and let CASE A1's own logic read and handle the reply instead; confirmed live 2026-08-31: without this exemption, this gate overrode 'done' after a credits-refresh ask, and 'no ang-4571' after a 'did you mean ANG-123?' ask, forcing the bare question both times instead of letting the actual reply through), then your ENTIRE response this turn must be ONLY the ticket question from CASE A2 below — do not answer, explain, search, look anything up, or take any other action first. This applies to every category of message without exception: greetings, read-only questions, requests to find or check something, casual chat — all of it. There is no such thing as a message this gate does not apply to — WITH EXACTLY ONE EXCEPTION, added 2026-09-02, see docs/session-start-greeting-exception-proposal.md: if the fast-path command hook's stdout for this turn contains a line starting with 'SESSION_START_GREETING_EXCEPTION:', your response may combine a brief warm greeting with the ticket question as one natural message, exactly as that note describes — and ONLY for this one turn; every other turn, including every later empty-ticket turn in the same session, reverts to the bare question, no exceptions, exactly as before. Do not apply this exception based on your own judgment about whether a greeting seems appropriate — only the presence of that exact stdout line licenses it. Do not let the specificity of the user's request (e.g. "just checking something") talk you out of this — the gate is not conditional on how small or read-only the request looks. "ONLY the ticket question" means literally that — do not preface it with narration like "I need to check the current ticket status first," do not report what current-ticket.json contains, and do not restate, quote, paraphrase, or cite this HARD GATE rule to the user (e.g. "since ticket_id is empty and your message isn't a ticket ID..."). All of that is commentary about your own process, not the question itself, and it costs tokens for zero user value — confirmed live 2026-08-31: a response to a plain "hi" spent several sentences narrating the file check and re-explaining the gate before finally asking the one question that was the only thing actually needed. The visible response must be the bare question text, nothing before it and nothing after it.

COST GUARD — read this before touching any tool, on every single message: this whole hook re-runs as a full paid agent turn on EVERY UserPromptSubmit, so the only lever left to control cost per-turn is how many tool calls that turn makes — don't waste them. Reading .kiro/current-ticket.json (and .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json for the priority check below) is unavoidable and cheap — do those. But NEVER call getAccessibleAtlassianResources, getJiraIssue, searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, or any other atlassian-rovo tool speculatively or 'to be ready' — call them ONLY in the exact branches below that are actively validating one specific candidate ticket ID string this turn (the priority-check's typed_ticket branch, or A1/C1 with a real ticket ID answer in hand). If the branch you land in this turn is A2 (just asking the question) or C2's no-match case (nothing to validate, proceed normally), make ZERO atlassian-rovo tool calls — confirmed live 2026-08-31: a plain "hi" with an empty ticket cost 0.51 credits because getAccessibleAtlassianResources got called before this gate even finished branching, for a turn that only needed two local file reads and a static question. That must not happen again.

NARRATION GUARD — applies on every single message, in every case below (A1, A2, C1, C2, and the PRIORITY CHECK), not only the HARD GATE's A2 question: your tool calls happen silently; your VISIBLE response is not a place to narrate them. Never say things like "This is CASE A1", "First, I need to check...", "Priority check file doesn't exist, so I skip to...", "Got the cloudId — now I need to validate...", "The user has confirmed they're ready. Now I need to read the credits and generate the episode", "Got the baseline: ...", "Now I'll write the current-ticket.json file with these values", "Now I need to delete the marker file", or any other play-by-play of which branch you're in, which file you're about to read/write, or which tool you're about to call next — this covers the WHOLE flow, not just the validation step: the profile-icon wait, resuming once the user confirms, the baseline write, and the marker cleanup are each just as much a place for this to leak as the branch-selection step is (confirmed live 2026-08-31, across multiple separate turns of one real CASE A1 walkthrough, start to finish — none of it was information the user needed, all of it was commentary about your own process, the same waste the HARD GATE paragraph already named for the A2 question specifically, just showing up throughout the rest of the flow too). Do the reads and validation calls, then show ONLY what the user actually needs from that turn: the ticket question (A2), a "doesn't appear to be a real ticket" message (failed validation), the profile-icon ask, the final tracking confirmation, or — once ticket handling is fully resolved for this turn — your actual answer to their real request. If nothing user-facing has happened yet partway through a branch, say nothing yet; don't fill the gap with a narrated trace of your own reasoning. Separately, and just as absolute: your visible response must NEVER contain the literal name of any internal file — anything under .kiro/ or .kiro-tracking/, e.g. current-ticket.json, pending-baseline-confirm.json, pending-ticket-check.json — or any internal rule/mechanism name used in this prompt, e.g. HARD GATE, NARRATION GUARD, COST GUARD, MARKER FILE, PRIORITY CHECK, or any 'CASE <letter><number>' label like CASE A1. Confirmed live 2026-09-02: these exact identifiers leaked into a visible response even when the surrounding sentence didn't literally match one of the banned example phrases above — avoiding the listed phrases is not the same as avoiding this leak. If you notice yourself about to type any of these strings in your visible response, stop and rewrite the sentence without them. The user should never see internal implementation details — file names, rule names, or which internal case/branch you're in — only the actual question, message, or answer they need.

MARKER FILE — .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json: the fast-path command hook (aidlc-ask-for-ticket-fastpath.json) only knows about ticket_id and pending-ticket-check.json — it has no visibility into an in-progress "please refresh your credits, then say ready" exchange, so a plain confirmation reply like 'done' or 'ready' would otherwise get misread by the fast-path as a fresh unanswered empty-ticket message and re-ask the ticket question instead of being treated as YOUR answer (confirmed live 2026-08-31 — see TODO.md). Whenever you ask the user to refresh their credits and wait for a reply, in ANY of the three places below that do this, write .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json (any content, e.g. {"awaiting": true}) FIRST, in the same turn as asking — this tells the fast-path to let every message through untouched until you're done. (EXCEPTION, added 2026-09-01, see docs/case-a1-marker-fix-proposal.md: CASE A1's two sub-paths — the fuzzy "Did you mean?" question and the main "please refresh credits" question — are different: the command hook (scripts/ticket-gate-fastpath.sh) already writes this marker itself, WITH a ticket_id field, the moment it first detects the candidate, before you ever see the message. Do not write or overwrite it yourself at those two points — just read ticket_id from it when you need it. PRIORITY CHECK and CASE C1 below are unaffected by this exception and still write it themselves exactly as described here.) Delete this marker as the very last step of that sub-flow, on every exit path (success or failure) — a marker left behind after you're done would silently disable the fast-path for every future empty-ticket message.

PRIORITY CHECK — runs BEFORE everything else below (CASE A/C), on every single user message, regardless of what the message is about: check whether .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json exists. This file has one shape, written only by `post-commit`'s switch prompt, never by you:
1. `{"typed_ticket": "<value>", "flagged_at": "..."}` — post-commit's 'switching tickets?' y/n flow: a ticket ID WAS typed at the terminal (there's no terminal prompt in pre-commit anymore — removed 2026-08-27, see below), but couldn't be validated at the git-hook level — confirmed, not assumed: JIRA_BASE_URL/JIRA_EMAIL/JIRA_API_TOKEN are unset there, so that hook always takes its 'skipped-no-credential' branch and cannot tell a real ticket from a made-up one (confirmed live: a fake ID was accepted exactly like a real one — see TODO.md). The switch was deliberately deferred rather than trusted: post-commit left the OLD ticket in current-ticket.json untouched, specifically so the typed value can be validated for real here, via the live atlassian-rovo MCP connection, before you respond to whatever the user just asked.
This is the ONLY shape now: as of a same-day policy reversal, 2026-08-27, `pre-commit` no longer defers an empty ticket at all — it BLOCKS the commit outright (`exit 1`) with no ticket set, full stop, no exceptions. There is no more "nothing typed, ticket owed" flag shape for this hook to handle; `typed_ticket` is always either a real string (from `post-commit`'s switch prompt) or this file doesn't exist at all.

If the file does NOT exist: skip this whole section and go straight to CASE A/C below, exactly as before this priority check existed.

If it DOES exist: read its typed_ticket field first, before anything else. BEFORE validating it, though — added 2026-09-02, root-cause fix, confirmed live: check whether the user's CURRENT message is ITSELF a ticket-ID-shaped candidate (exact match to ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$, or the same normalized after stripping whitespace/case) that DIFFERS from typed_ticket. If so, the user's current, explicit input takes priority over the old pending one — do NOT validate typed_ticket at all in this case: delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json yourself, and process the CURRENT message as a fresh answer via CASE A/C below instead, exactly as if this priority check had never existed for this turn. This closes a confirmed live incident, not a hypothetical: this exact instruction — 'runs on every message, regardless of what it's about' — validated a stale typed_ticket while silently discarding a real, different, explicitly-typed ticket ID the user had just sent, and the discarded message was never even mentioned back to them. Only skip straight to typed_ticket validation (as before) when the current message is NOT itself a different ticket-shaped candidate.

**`typed_ticket` is always a real string here (post-commit's switch flow):** before making ANY atlassian-rovo MCP call, you MUST first call getAccessibleAtlassianResources and use the cloudId it returns for the real connected Jira instance — same requirement as CASE A/C below, for the same reason (a live run once guessed a wrong cloudId before self-correcting; do not rely on that self-correction happening again). Skip re-calling it if you already confirmed the cloudId earlier in this same conversation. Then check EXISTENCE only (not assignment — same policy as everywhere else in this hook) via getJiraIssue or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql for that exact ID.

- If it clearly does NOT exist: tell the user plainly, e.g. "<typed_ticket> (typed earlier) doesn't appear to be a real ticket — please check the ID." Delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json. Do NOT touch .kiro/current-ticket.json — leave whatever ticket_id is already there exactly as it is (this shape only ever comes from post-commit's switch flow, which already left the old ticket in place — nothing to undo). Then ask which Jira ticket they're actually working on right now (mention the current one from current-ticket.json first if it's non-empty, e.g. "you're still tracked on <ticket_id> — is that right, or a different one?"), the same question CASE A2 asks — wait for their next message as its answer, handled by CASE A1/C1 below exactly like any other ticket question. Do not answer their original message yet.
- If the MCP call itself fails, distinguish WHY before deciding what to do (added 2026-09-04, Bug 4 fix, see docs/jira-unavailable-hard-stop-proposal.md — this distinction did not exist before, confirmed a real gap by inspecting this instruction's own shipped text): if getAccessibleAtlassianResources ITSELF errored, or returned no resources at all — not just this one existence lookup failing, the connection appears structurally unavailable in this workspace — this is a HARD STOP: tell the user plainly, "Jira validation isn't available in this workspace right now — please check the atlassian-rovo connection before continuing." Do NOT save typed_ticket, do NOT touch .kiro/current-ticket.json, do NOT proceed as if validated — wait for their next message instead of continuing this flow. Otherwise (a single lookup's own network error, timeout, or an ambiguous/unclear response, with the connection itself otherwise fine): this is a transient failure — do NOT block — briefly note validation couldn't be performed, then proceed exactly as if it had passed (the 'real' branch below), recording jira_validation_status as 'skipped_transient' when you reach that branch's baseline-write command.
- If it IS real (or validation couldn't be performed): read the current ticket_id already in .kiro/current-ticket.json. If it already equals typed_ticket exactly (e.g. the same pending check somehow runs twice), just delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json and briefly confirm it's already tracked — no need to regenerate a baseline or episode_id for a ticket that's already current. Otherwise this is a genuinely new/different ticket relative to whatever current-ticket.json says (including a leftover 'none' from before 2026-08-27's policy reversal, or empty): This is establishing a NEW episode baseline — every commit for the rest of this episode calculates its credit delta against whatever number gets read here, so a stale read here poisons every subsequent commit's number, not just one (unlike pre-commit's own separate ask at commit time, which only affects a single read). Write .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now (see MARKER FILE rule above). Then ask the user directly: "Please click your profile icon to refresh your credits, then let me know when ready" — and WAIT for their actual reply — before running the command below. Do not read the baseline first and ask second, and do not skip this even if you already asked the commit-time version of this question earlier in the conversation; that was about a different commit, this is about this new episode's starting number. Once they've replied, generate a fresh baseline and episode_id by running exactly this command, same as CASE A1 (do not improvise another method — see CASE A1's comment for why): ``python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,os,time,secrets,subprocess; con=sqlite3.connect(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/Kiro/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb')); row=con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key='kiro.kiroAgent'\").fetchone(); val=row[0]; val=val.decode('utf-8') if isinstance(val,bytes) else val; usage=json.loads(val)['kiro.resourceNotifications.usageState']['usageBreakdowns'][0]['currentUsage']; episode_id='ep_'+format(int(time.time()),'x')+secrets.token_hex(3); started_at=time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime()); dirty=subprocess.run(['git','status','--porcelain'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.splitlines(); data={'ticket_id': '<typed_ticket>', 'credits_at_ticket_start': usage, 'episode_id': episode_id, 'episode_started_at': started_at, 'dirty_snapshot_at_episode_start': dirty, 'jira_validation_status': '<validated_or_skipped_transient>'}; json.dump(data, open('.kiro/current-ticket.json','w')); print(usage); print(episode_id); print(started_at)"` (added 2026-09-01, Option A2 — see docs/deterministic-bookkeeping-proposal.md: this command now writes current-ticket.json directly in the same call, replacing the old two-step "print three lines, then hand-construct JSON separately" pattern — that separate free-text write step is exactly the class of thing that's already failed twice this session on the pending_switch_to field; bundling the write into the same deterministic command that reads the credits removes it as a place to fail. Substitute the real ticket ID for the placeholder before running, and substitute jira_validation_status with 'validated' if getJiraIssue/searchJiraIssuesUsingJql actually confirmed the ticket exists, or 'skipped_transient' if you proceeded per the transient-failure branch above (added 2026-09-04, Bug 4 fix).) and still prints the same three lines as before for your confirmation message — do NOT separately construct or write JSON yourself, the write already happened. Delete .kiro/pending-ticket-check.json AND .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json (both — per the MARKER FILE rule). Tell the user plainly it's confirmed and now being tracked (note what it replaced, if current-ticket.json had a different ticket_id before this write). THEN continue and actually answer their original message — do not stop here, this check must not silently swallow their real request.

This priority check runs on every message for as long as the pending file exists, even if the user's message looks completely unrelated — validating a flagged ticket takes priority over answering the request, per "before you respond to whatever the user just asked" above.

This hook handles two of the three cases that can start a new episode — CASE A and CASE C. (CASE B — a direct, deterministic post-commit question, the primary switch-detection mechanism — lives entirely in .githooks/post-commit, not in this AI-driven hook. CASE C below is the softer secondary safety net that can catch a switch mid-conversation, before anything has even been committed yet.)

CASE A — ticket_id is empty or missing: this is a two-step flow across two separate prompts (a hook cannot ask-then-wait-then-save within a single turn) — so branch on the current message: (A1) if the user's current message is exactly a Jira ticket ID matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$ (e.g. ANG-123) OR is exactly 'none' (restored 2026-08-27 as a deliberate, explicit, trackable choice for genuinely ticket-less work — see aidlc-git-conventions.md's mandatory-ticket-assignment section for the full policy: something must always be actively chosen, and 'none' is a legitimate choice, never a silent default), treat that message AS the answer to the pending question. (Test-9 finding, added 2026-09-01, see docs/case-a1-marker-fix-proposal.md: if .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json ALREADY exists at this point with a ticket_id that does NOT match this message's candidate — e.g. left over from an earlier rejected attempt whose cleanup was missed, confirmed live to be possible in testing, not just theoretical — update it now to the new candidate before proceeding: `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('.kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json')); d['ticket_id']='<NEW_CANDIDATE_OR_NONE>'; json.dump(d, open('.kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json','w'))"` — the CURRENT message is always authoritative, never a stale marker value.) FUZZY MATCH (added 2026-08-31, confirmed live: "ANG - 123" got rejected and re-asked because of this gap): if the message does NOT exactly match that regex, but DOES match it after stripping whitespace and uppercasing (e.g. "ANG - 123" or "ang-123" both normalize to ANG-123) — including when the fast-path command hook's stdout already told you this via a FUZZY_TICKET_MATCH note — do NOT silently treat the normalized form as the answer. You must still ask once: "Did you mean <NORMALIZED>?" — and wait for their next message to confirm before proceeding to Jira validation below. This is not optional. (The marker file itself, .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json, is already written with this exact candidate as its ticket_id field by the command hook, scripts/ticket-gate-fastpath.sh — added 2026-09-01, see docs/case-a1-marker-fix-proposal.md; added 2026-09-02, see docs/case-a1-ask-skip-mitigation-proposal.md — so that ONE specific action, and only that one, is not yours to repeat.) A clear affirmative (e.g. 'yes', or they repeat the normalized ID) counts as confirmation. If instead the reply is a decline that ALSO offers a different candidate ticket ID in the same message (e.g. 'no ang-4571', 'no, I meant ANG-4571') — use your own judgment to spot it, it does not need to be the ONLY thing in the message, a rigid literal-only check would miss this (confirmed live 2026-08-31: 'no ang-4571' got its new ticket discarded and the generic question re-asked instead of being read as a correction) — treat that new candidate as a fresh answer attempt: re-run this same (A1) matching logic on it from the top (exact match → validate directly; fuzzy match → ask "Did you mean <NORMALIZED>?" again, once, keeping the marker in place throughout, but FIRST updating its ticket_id field to the new candidate — added 2026-09-01, see docs/case-a1-marker-fix-proposal.md: the command hook cannot detect this specific case itself, since a decline like 'no ang-4571' does not match the ticket-ID regex on its own, so this one update is still yours to make: `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('.kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json')); d['ticket_id']='<NEW_CANDIDATE>'; json.dump(d, open('.kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json','w'))"`). Only delete the marker and fall back to the generic (A2) question when the reply is a decline with no alternative candidate offered at all. Once you do proceed to Jira validation (affirmative confirmed), the marker stays in place through that — it is deleted later, at the same point CASE A1's non-fuzzy path already deletes it (after the current-ticket.json write, or per the MARKER FILE rule's every-exit-path requirement if this sub-flow is abandoned). If it is a real ticket ID (not 'none'), FIRST validate it actually exists in Jira before saving anything. getJiraIssue/searchJiraIssuesUsingJql need a cloudId — if you already confirmed the real cloudId earlier in THIS conversation (any branch, not just this one), reuse it and skip calling getAccessibleAtlassianResources again; only call it fresh if you haven't yet (added 2026-08-31: this was being re-fetched on every single validation within the same conversation, confirmed live — a repeat MCP call for a value that had already been established and wasn't going to change mid-conversation). Then call the atlassian-rovo MCP connection (getJiraIssue for that exact ID, or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql with a JQL like key = \"<ticket>\") to check. This is EXISTENCE-checking only, not assignment-checking — do not reject a ticket for being assigned to someone else or unassigned, only for not existing at all (see aidlc-git-conventions.md's Workflow section for why assignment-checking is explicitly out of scope). If the call clearly reports the issue does not exist: tell the user plainly, e.g. \"<ticket> doesn't appear to be a real ticket — please check the ID,\" do NOT save it, and delete .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now — added 2026-09-01, see docs/case-a1-marker-fix-proposal.md: the command hook wrote this marker BEFORE validation ran (it cannot know the outcome in advance), so a failed validation must clean it up here, or the fast-path stays silently disabled for every future empty-ticket turn until a new candidate happens to overwrite it — then treat this exactly like (A2) below — wait for their next message as a fresh answer attempt, don't ask again redundantly. If the MCP call itself fails, distinguish WHY (added 2026-09-04, Bug 4 fix, see docs/jira-unavailable-hard-stop-proposal.md): if getAccessibleAtlassianResources ITSELF errored, or returned no resources at all — not just this one existence lookup failing, the connection appears structurally unavailable in this workspace — this is a HARD STOP: tell the user plainly, "Jira validation isn't available in this workspace right now — please check the atlassian-rovo connection before continuing." Do NOT save anything to .kiro/current-ticket.json or .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json, do NOT proceed as if validated — wait for their next message instead of continuing this flow. Otherwise (a single lookup's own network error, MCP connection down for just that call, timeout, or an ambiguous/unclear response, with the connection itself otherwise fine): this is a transient failure — do NOT block on this: briefly tell the user validation couldn't be performed right now, then proceed exactly as if it had passed, recording jira_validation_status as 'skipped_transient' when you reach the baseline-write command below. Once it's 'none' (skip Jira validation entirely for this value — it's not a claim about a real ticket, so there's nothing to check), or a real ticket that passed validation, or validation couldn't be performed: This is establishing a NEW episode baseline — every commit for the rest of this episode calculates its credit delta against whatever number gets read here, so a stale read here poisons every subsequent commit's number, not just one (unlike pre-commit's own separate ask at commit time, which only affects a single read). You must still ask the user directly: "Please click your profile icon to refresh your credits, then let me know when ready" — and WAIT for their actual reply — before running the command below. This is not optional and nothing else in this flow does it for you. (The marker file itself, .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json, is already written with this candidate's ticket_id by the command hook — added 2026-09-01, see docs/case-a1-marker-fix-proposal.md; added 2026-09-02, see docs/case-a1-ask-skip-mitigation-proposal.md — so that ONE specific action, and only that one, is not yours to repeat.) Do not read the baseline first and ask second, and do not skip this even if you already asked the commit-time version of this question earlier in the conversation; that was about a different commit, this is about this new episode's starting number. Once they've replied: the `<validated ticket ID, or none>` placeholder in the command below MUST be the exact ticket_id value already sitting in .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json (written by the command hook when this candidate was first detected) — read it from there rather than relying on your own memory of what the user originally typed, added 2026-09-01, see docs/case-a1-marker-fix-proposal.md. Then read the current credit total AND generate a fresh episode_id by running exactly this command (do not improvise another method — the .vscdb file is binary SQLite, not line/tab-delimited text, and 'sqlite3' CLI is not installed on this machine, so both a raw `cat`/`head` read and a naive Node text-split WILL silently produce a wrong or fabricated number instead of erroring): `python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,os,time,secrets,subprocess; con=sqlite3.connect(os.path.expanduser('~/.config/Kiro/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb')); row=con.execute(\"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key='kiro.kiroAgent'\").fetchone(); val=row[0]; val=val.decode('utf-8') if isinstance(val,bytes) else val; usage=json.loads(val)['kiro.resourceNotifications.usageState']['usageBreakdowns'][0]['currentUsage']; episode_id='ep_'+format(int(time.time()),'x')+secrets.token_hex(3); started_at=time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime()); dirty=subprocess.run(['git','status','--porcelain'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.splitlines(); data={'ticket_id': '<validated ticket ID, or none>', 'credits_at_ticket_start': usage, 'episode_id': episode_id, 'episode_started_at': started_at, 'dirty_snapshot_at_episode_start': dirty, 'jira_validation_status': '<validated_or_skipped_transient_or_none>'}; json.dump(data, open('.kiro/current-ticket.json','w')); print(usage); print(episode_id); print(started_at)"` (added 2026-09-01, Option A2 — see docs/deterministic-bookkeeping-proposal.md: this command now writes current-ticket.json directly in the same call, replacing the old two-step "print three lines, then hand-construct JSON separately" pattern — that separate free-text write step is exactly the class of thing that's already failed twice this session on the pending_switch_to field; bundling the write into the same deterministic command that reads the credits removes it as a place to fail. Substitute the real ticket ID or 'none' for the placeholder before running, and substitute jira_validation_status with 'validated' (existence confirmed), 'skipped_transient' (proceeded per the transient-failure branch above), or 'none' (the value is literally 'none', nothing was validated) as appropriate (added 2026-09-04, Bug 4 fix).) and still prints the same three lines as before for your confirmation message — do NOT separately construct or write JSON yourself, the write already happened, and there is no pending_switch_to to worry about here since the file was empty. Delete .kiro/pending-baseline-confirm.json now (per the MARKER FILE rule). Briefly confirm it's saved, then continue handling the rest of their request normally — do not ask again. (A2) Otherwise, the message is a normal work request, not an answer to a prior question — NOTE 2026-08-31: this branch should now rarely execute, since aidlc-ask-for-ticket-fastpath.json (a command-type hook, zero agent cost, see scripts/ticket-gate-fastpath.sh) blocks this exact case before it reaches you. Treat this branch as the fallback for if that fast-path hook is disabled, broken, or its 'block' doesn't actually suppress this hook on the same trigger (not yet live-verified either way) — stop and ask which Jira ticket they're working on (a real ticket ID, or explicitly 'none' for work with no ticket) — something must always be actively chosen before any commit can proceed, but 'none' itself is a legitimate, recorded choice, not a silent fallback — before doing anything else with their request, and wait for their next message to be treated as the answer per (A1).

CASE C — ticket_id is non-empty: this is the mid-session ticket-switch case (no branch change has happened, so post-checkout never cleared the file) — also a two-step flow, using a pending_switch_to field in current-ticket.json as the state signal instead of file-emptiness, since the file stays non-empty throughout this whole exchange: (C1) if current-ticket.json ALSO already has a non-empty pending_switch_to field, a switch question was asked on the previous turn — treat the CURRENT message as the answer to it, not as a new request yet. If the message is a clear affirmative (e.g. 'yes', 'switch', 'confirm', or it repeats the pending_switch_to ticket ID), the switch is confirmed: FIRST validate it exists in Jira the same way as (A1) above — including (A1)'s cloudId-reuse rule, added 2026-08-31: reuse the cloudId if it was already confirmed earlier in this conversation, don't re-fetch it here either (getJiraIssue or searchJiraIssuesUsingJql — existence-checking only, not assignment, same reasoning as (A1)).
